market.outlook: Cautiously positive for Colombia, particularly for a professional treatment-plus-maintenance proposition. ANDI reports that beauty and personal care reached USD 3.565 billion in 2025, growing 8.6% over 2024, and identifies hair products among the categories leading sales. These are broader beauty/personal-care figures, not the size or growth rate of professional straighteners. Source: https://www.andi.com.co/Home/Noticia/18027-industria-cosmetica-y-de-aseo-domestico. Local commercial evidence is more specific: Skalante markets Brazilian straightening systems alongside home care, and Haskell recruits professional wholesale customers. That supports category/channel relevance, but no reliable Colombia-specific forecast for LQ's exact segment was found. Competition is established, and a new brand must demonstrate differentiation, repeatable salon results and commercially workable local pricing. LQ's website supports professional straightening-to-nutrition positioning and reseller support, but does not establish Colombian regulatory readiness or an export programme.
market.buyerDynamics: The documented channels combine professional wholesale, salon supply and consumer e-commerce. Skalante pairs Brazilian straightening products with technical advice and post-treatment maintenance; Haskell recruits salons and beauty businesses through a wholesale programme; Star supplies haircare and other beauty categories to salons and distributors. Buyers can approach these businesses through published WhatsApp, email and online catalogues. For LQ, distinguish a distributor's ability to stock professional products from its authority to appoint an imported brand: ask who approves new suppliers and which entity imports. Public listings establish assortment, not purchase intent. Existing brand mandates also matter: WOW has an OLAPLEX-specific official-import position, while Haskell Colombia and Italian Beauty Concept are branded distribution channels rather than demonstrated independent multi-brand importers. market.outlook: Uganda is a plausible but competitive market for Kanechom’s treatment masks, leave-in creams, oils and shampoo/conditioner packs. Euromonitor’s Uganda overview identifies digitally engaged young consumers, premiumisation, styling agents and salon-professional haircare as growth themes, while also highlighting price sensitivity. Its channel commentary favours broad retail availability alongside professional education—not a salon-only launch. The recent Venus distributor appointment and stylist workshop demonstrate active brand-building in the category. Kanechom’s product relevance is an assessment, not evidence of established Ugandan demand for the brand or Brazilian haircare specifically. No verified market-size figure, growth rate, Brazil-origin import total or current local professional-tier price benchmark was established.
market.buyerDynamics: The evidenced route combines importer/distributor representation, wholesale replenishment, van delivery to smaller retailers, modern trade and salon recommendation. Charms describes countrywide van sales to retail outlets and corner shops; Delight supplies shopping stores and salons. Euromonitor’s Uganda overview says small local grocers lead sales while supermarkets gain urban share, with professional collaborations and e-commerce supporting discovery. Grow Well’s own profile names Carrefour, Fraine, Jazz, Embassy and Millennium among modern-trade channels; these are supplier claims, not independently confirmed customer relationships. For Kanechom, sell the distributor a commercially workable assortment and replenishment plan, then support its retailer and salon sell-through. Purchasing authority, competing-brand obligations, landed margins and willingness to launch must be confirmed separately from channel fit.
importSignals: Dembe explicitly identifies itself as an importer and distributor, and publishes authorised Uganda distribution for L’Oréal hair and skincare. This is strong category-access evidence, but not evidence of an available purchasing mandate for Kanechom. https://dembe.com/company-profile ; https://www.dembe.com/brand/loreal

Mukisa explicitly advertises importation, distribution and retail of haircare alongside skincare, perfumes and cosmetics. This is a relevant, undated operating claim; specific brands and recent shipments remain unverified. https://mukisaholdings.com/

SkyBirds states that it imports FMCG from India, Dubai, the UK and Italy, including personal care. Its published Simple and Aveeno cosmetics listings establish adjacent-category activity, not a verified haircare assortment. https://www.skybirds.co.ug/

Grow Well’s corporate profile, published in its July 2026 document directory, describes direct sourcing from Egypt and the UAE. Separate reporting documents its appointment for PZ Cussons’ Imperial Leather and Venus Haircare; an October 2026 Venus stylist workshop provides recent category-activity evidence. These sources do not disclose shipment records. https://growwellug.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Corporate-Profile-Grow-Well-Uganda-Limited.pdf ; https://www.ugnewsline.com/growwell-unveiled-as-pz-cussons-distributor ; https://mbu.ug/2026/10/07/venus-haircare-relaunches-with-ugandan-salonists-at-the-center-as-new-rebrand-answers-what-consumers-asked-for

Recommended sales sequence: verify professional-brand imports and portfolio eligibility; identify the new-brand decision-maker; offer a technical evaluation; then negotiate a launch order. Multifunctional use should be demonstrated through documented application protocols, not promised as an unverified performance claim. No reviewed source establishes willingness to buy LQ.
